references.text: Stephen quotes this verse directly in his speech, describing how the Israelites rejected Moses with the words: 'Who made you a ruler and judge over us? Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?'
Stephen again refers to the rejection of Moses as 'ruler and judge,' showing how God still sent him as both leader and deliverer.
The context for the cross-reference - Moses killing the Egyptian is mentioned in verse 14.
Moses' fear mentioned in verse 14 leads directly to his flight from Pharaoh to Midian.
Joseph's brothers rejected his leadership with similar words: 'Will you be king over us?' - the same pattern of rejecting a future deliverer.
Jesus uses similar wording when he asks, 'Who made me a judge or arbitrator over you?' - possibly an allusion to the Moses text.
Dathan and Abiram challenged Moses' authority in a similar way, asking if he intended to make himself ruler over them.
Thematic parallel: Repeated challenges to Moses' leadership and authority from the people.
Direct allusion: Jesus links his persecution to Moses' experience in Egypt (the death threat from the people).
